newsitem.title: USA: L.A. municipal utility says alliance plan on track.
newsitem.headline: L.A. municipal utility says alliance plan on track.

text.p: The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) expects to decide next month between Duke/Louis Dreyfus, Enron Corp and PacifiCorp as a power marketing partner, a spokeswoman said Tuesday.

LADWP board members meeting today said a recent request by Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan for the utility to examine an alliance with neighboring utilities would be followed up, but the existing alliance plans will go forward, spokeswoman Karen Denne said.
Riordan had suggested LADWP look at a partnership with Edison International's Southern California Edison Co or Pacific Enterprises, parent of Southern California Gas Co, she said.
Denne said some sort of alliance with a regulated utility may be a possiblity, but it is too early to be certain.
California will begin to open its electricity market to competition in January 1998.

Earlier this month, Enron was chosen by Northern California Power Agency to manage power supply and energy sales for the agency, which groups 15 primarily municipal members serving customers in northern and central California.
Late last year, Portland General Electric Co, which plans to merge with Enron, was chosen by the city of Palm Springs, Calif., to supply its power needs starting in 1998.
